name: Market abuse (insider dealing, wash trading, pump-and-dump) as a predicate and laundering vehicle
description: Securities and token markets are manipulated or exploited with inside information to generate illicit profit, and the same trading channels are then used to disguise the source of other criminal funds by manufacturing apparent trading gains or losses. Typical vehicles are thinly traded issuers, newly listed tokens, linked or nominee accounts and coordinated promotion. The proceeds are quickly withdrawn, moved offshore or converted, so surveillance and AML teams need shared visibility of trading behaviour and money movement.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Securities Sector, 2009
European Union, Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 on market abuse (Market Abuse Regulation), 2014
FATF, Virtual Assets: Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, 2020

exposure.rationale: Trading accounts and token venues; proceeds moved offshore or into virtual assets.

indicators.name: Wash or matched trades between connected parties
indicators.canon: Wash or matched trades between connected parties
indicators.desc: Assets or securities are traded repeatedly between linked accounts or wallets at unrealistic prices.
indicators.ctx: Repeated buying and selling of the same instrument or token between connected accounts at no real change of beneficial ownership, creating false volume or a price trail that justifies deposits and withdrawals.
indicators.fp: Collectors moving assets between own wallets.

indicators.name: Trading in low-liquidity securities with unrelated parties
indicators.canon: Trading in low-liquidity securities with unrelated parties
indicators.desc: Illiquid instruments used to move value.
indicators.ctx: Concentrated dealing in thinly traded or micro-cap issuers where a few accounts can set the price and counterparties appear to be pre-arranged.

indicators.name: Newly established customer with rapid high-value activity
indicators.canon: Newly established customer with rapid high-value activity
indicators.desc: A recently formed customer with little history or track record quickly records large turnover or trades in high-value or restricted goods.
indicators.ctx: Accounts opened and funded shortly before a promoted issuer or token moves, then used almost entirely to accumulate that one holding.
indicators.fp: Genuine start-ups or fast-growing businesses can scale quickly; test against business plan and evidence of operations.

indicators.name: Collusive purchases between related buyer and seller accounts
indicators.canon: Collusive purchases between related buyer and seller accounts
indicators.desc: Accounts sharing devices or funding sources transact with each other to create revenue.
indicators.ctx: Related buyer and seller accounts on a trading venue, NFT marketplace or token exchange, linked by device, funding source or wallet, trade with each other to fabricate demand.

indicators.name: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt
indicators.canon: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt
indicators.desc: Incoming funds are quickly sent abroad or converted to virtual assets soon after being credited.
indicators.ctx: Sale proceeds from a spike in price are moved offshore or into virtual assets within days, before the price retraces or a regulator or venue intervenes.
indicators.fp: Genuine international payments or planned crypto purchases by established customers.

indicators.name: Shell entity with no operating footprint
indicators.canon: Shell entity with no operating footprint
indicators.desc: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
indicators.ctx: The issuer or promoted company has no real operations, staff or revenue, so its securities have little value beyond the promotional narrative.
indicators.fp: Start-ups, holding companies and special-purpose vehicles may legitimately lack a footprint.

indicators.name: Trading ahead of material non-public announcements
indicators.canon: Trading ahead of material non-public announcements
indicators.desc: A customer or linked accounts take unusually large or well-timed positions shortly before a price-sensitive event such as a takeover, results release or listing decision, then close out soon after the news.
indicators.ctx: Core insider-dealing signal, and a route for turning inside information into spendable proceeds that are then banked or moved.
indicators.fp: Skilled analysis of public information, sector-wide positioning, scheduled portfolio rebalancing or pre-planned option exercises can look similar. Look for repeat timing and links to insiders.

indicators.name: Promotion campaign alongside concentrated selling by connected holders
indicators.canon: Promotion campaign alongside concentrated selling by connected holders
indicators.desc: Coordinated social-media, messaging-group or cold-call promotion of a low-priced instrument coincides with unusual buying volume while a small group of connected holders sells into the rise.
indicators.ctx: Defines the pump-and-dump pattern and links the promoters to the beneficiaries of the exit trades.
indicators.fp: Genuine news, index inclusion or legitimate investor-relations activity can raise interest and volume. Weight the link between promoters and sellers.

indicators.name: Orders placed and cancelled without intent to execute
indicators.canon: Orders placed and cancelled without intent to execute
indicators.desc: Large orders are repeatedly entered and withdrawn before execution, or small orders are layered, in a way that moves the visible price or depth in favour of positions held elsewhere.
indicators.ctx: Manipulative price-formation behaviour that precedes a profitable trade and is only visible in order-level data.
indicators.fp: Market makers and algorithmic strategies legitimately cancel at high rates. Compare to the customer's stated strategy and the benefit on related positions.

indicators.name: Token deployer or insider wallets distributing holdings into promoted price rise
indicators.canon: Token deployer or insider wallets distributing holdings into promoted price rise
indicators.desc: Wallets linked to a token's creator, early allocation or liquidity pool move large balances to exchanges or fresh wallets as promotion drives the price up, often followed by liquidity removal.
indicators.ctx: Crypto equivalent of insiders selling into a pump, including rug-pull style exits.
indicators.fp: Vesting schedules, treasury management and disclosed team allocations can involve similar transfers. Check against published token schedules.

added.subject: Add 9 typologies from reference review (market abuse, complicit FI, sham legal, sports, freeports, pensions, transfer pricing, scam compounds, cross-border mules)
